facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 木_比肩 (Wood carrying The Twin). Persona The Twin (比肩). Definition line: "Same nature, same register, the standard you hold yourself to". Keyword Independence, charge steady, poles catalyst Self-trust / friction Isolation. Family function: Body. Cost dimension: the standard held to oneself; company that truly matches is rare. Arena: mirrors, stride, equal measure, walking beside. Classical portrait: same nature, same register; the standard held to oneself; self-reliance that can wall others out. Ruled domains: Peers, Independence, Self-reliance. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 劫财.
Element arena: Wood (trunk, branch, root, grain, growth, the forest). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Wood. structural_interaction seed: "Reach amplifying reach — developmental instinct without definition or counterforce".
- k2_overview: "Your Wood moves as the Twin: growth that stands beside others without leaning on them. You rise the way two trees share a hillside, close enough to shelter each other, rooted enough to stand alone. Ambition, for you, is upward and personal. You measure yourself against your own last season, and quietly against the tree beside you."
- k2_functional: "Your stamina is vegetal: quiet, continuous, renewed by daylight and outdoor air."
- adj_chips: {"friction":["Standoffish","Stubborn","Slow to change"],"catalyst":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Peers":"Your peers are the grove: people growing the same direction at their own speeds. Comparison is your fertilizer and your poison, so use the grove for shade and shelter, and race only your own rings.","Independence":"Wood independence is having your own soil: your plot, your craft, your income no one else waters. Secure it early. You bend badly when planted in someone else’s garden.","Self-reliance":"You hold yourself up through storms that flatten louder people, and you rarely mention the wind afterward. Let someone stake you when you are newly transplanted. It is not dependence. It is horticulture."}

  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 木_劫财 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Fast-climbing","Gutsy","Rivalry-fueled"],"friction":["Overreaching","Turf-guarding","Impulsive"]}
- Sibling cell 木_劫财 catalyst row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Upward is your body’s default direction, and speed is its signature. New job, new ladder, new wall: you find the holds faster than anyone expects, and you are halfway up before the group finishes stretching. Height that takes others years takes you seasons."

Core element Wood, energy element Wood. Law: Wood and Wood are the same element (the self pair). Relative to the core the energy is the self, so Wood is this core's Body. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Wood core that shows Wood on the catalyst pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The catalyst pole of Wood as the Body is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: compliment. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 木_木's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: Doing it alone comes before any plan you make. Owing nobody feels safer to you, so you do the whole thing yourself sooner than hand off a piece. Let someone carry a corner, because you do just as well with company beside you.

value_b.text: Where help is offered, you do it alone anyway. Needing nothing is a quiet pride, so you do it yourself ahead of leaning on a peer. Accept one offer a month, since doing everything alone costs you every favour you turn away.

value.text: Your own two hands are the only ones you count on. Doing it alone matters more than being carried, and that keeps your friends outside every hard week. Let one peer in, since doing it alone costs them the chance to matter to you.

value.text: Fast or slow around you, you move at your own speed. Being your own clock keeps you steady, since a borrowed pace never feels like yours. You keep your own pace ahead of catching the group, and some days the group is worth catching.

value_b.text: You set your own pace and keep it, fast day or slow. Steadiness is what you trust most, and you would sooner arrive late at your speed than early at another's. You reach a few chances late and take the rest at your own pace.

value.text: Where a sprint would get you in, you keep your pace instead. You would sooner be late on your terms than rushed on another's, since borrowed tempo is never yours. You lose the chance that needed a sprint, and that pace was yours to choose.

value.text: Your pace is one thing you never change for company. Keeping your own speed matters more than keeping step, and that leaves your people waiting or going ahead. Match a friend's step once a week, because you cost them the company of moving together.

value.text: You are the same person in any company. Holding one standard for yourself keeps your footing, since a new shape for each group would cost you your measure. You stay consistent ahead of fitting in, and fitting in once in a while costs you nothing.

value_b.text: Whatever the company, you hold the same standard. Being a single person everywhere lets you trust yourself, because a self that bends cannot be measured. You keep your shape rather than borrow a looser one and pay in the ease of blending in.

value.text: Whenever the moment calls for a softer you, you show up as usual. You would rather stay the same than be liked for a performance, since an adjusted self is hard to trust. You miss the closeness that bending buys, and a little is allowed.

value.text: Holding yourself to one standard means holding your friends to it. Staying the same matters more than meeting anyone halfway, and that leaves no slack for an off day. Bend for one friend this month, since consistency costs them the mercy of an easier you.
